data.narrative:
Voyant Photonics is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Chris Phare and Steven Miller, having raised $23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor companies, including same-stage comparables SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression anchors to the $23M raised as a proxy for pre-money value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implying $46M. Peer-median valuation uses the three same-sector, same-stage comparables, yielding a median of $2.3B with a range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 18.4x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) is not applicable without disclosed revenue data.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $39M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide disparity reflects material uncertainty around Voyant's competitive positioning relative to peers. The stage-progression method produces a substantially lower estimate, suggesting either that the $23M raised reflects conservative financing or that peer valuations in this sector command significant premiums independent of capital deployed. Key uncertainties include product maturity, addressable market validation, and whether peer multiples reflect genuine commercial differentiation or exuberant frontier-tech valuations.
